title: Software Project
summary: There is no exam. At the end of the project the software project committee grades the team on exploration, product, process, and the final presentation with Q&A, and the writing lecturer grades the report. Every part needs at least a 5.0 and the combined grade at least a 5.8, and only the report can be repaired. To be admitted you need CSE11B, CSE100, CSE13B and CSE12B, the SP Bootcamp and a registration on Project Forum.

basis.note: The archive holds no exam papers: the course is assessed as a project. What is said here comes from the official course description, the course and report rubrics, and the TU Write report guide.

format.mode: Team project for an external client, assessed on the final report, the code and its tests, and an on-campus final presentation with a live demo and Q&A
format.duration: The whole of quarter 4, full time (15 EC, about 42 hours a week); no timed exam
format.structure: Deliverables: a project plan; a working product with tests and documentation (code comments, README with dependencies, build steps and APIs); a final report of at most 12,000 words from introduction to conclusion, uploaded with a change log and an AI-use document; and the final presentation. Before that: a draft report, a self-assessment, writing assignments, a code of conduct and an individual reflection.
format.grading: Exploration 20 percent, product 35 percent, report 15 percent (graded by the writing lecturer), process 20 percent, presentation and Q&A 10 percent. Each part needs 5.0 and the total 5.8. The report scores ten criteria at 1, 4, 7 or 10 points, grade = points / 10. A failed report can be resubmitted for at most 6.0; the other parts have no repair. One student's grade can be lowered for too little contribution.
format.aids: Generative AI may be used for the report if you declare how in the preface footnote and describe the tools and prompts in a separate document.

trends: From 2026-27 the course code is CSE200 instead of CSE2000, and the entry requirements are new: CSE11B, CSE100, CSE13B and CSE12B plus the mandatory SP Bootcamp.
strategy: Plan by the weights: the [[product is the largest part (35 percent)]], judged on systematic quality assurance with several methods, sound architecture and workflows, fit with the client's problem, and documentation.

Exploration is a fifth of the grade: make the problem analysis, the risks, the justified requirements and the research behind your design choices visible in the report, since the committee reads them there.

The process grade rewards a plan you follow and adjust, your own initiative, critical reflection on your choices and good contact with TA, client and coach; keep planning records and meeting notes as evidence.
The difficulty of the assignment and the novelty of the solution count in the grade, so explain in the report and presentation what made the problem hard.
Use the draft round: say which parts you want feedback on, score the draft yourselves with the rubric, bring three questions to the draft meeting, then log every change for the final upload.
Write each report chapter for its reader: the CEO reads summary, introduction, problem and conclusion; the CTO reads requirements, design and testing; the next team reads the appendices.
Rehearse the presentation so it covers research, design and product, the demo runs smoothly, and every member can answer questions on any part of the work.
pitfalls: A [[partial grade below 5.0 fails the whole team]], however good the other parts are, and only the report has a second chance, [[capped at 6.0]].

Report killer criteria: [[a plagiarism issue, a missing AI declaration, a missing required part, missing assignment content or exceeding the word limit]] makes the report insufficient at once, and the new version counts as the resit.
The report fails if [[more than two of its ten criteria score poor, or more than four score mediocre or lower]], even when the total looks fine.
Too few or badly handled sources: fewer than 10 references or fewer than 5 scientific ones, citations that do not match the list, or a mix of styles.
Leaving out appendices the guide asks for: the full requirements table with which ones were met, and a division-of-labour overview of at most one A4.

The Q&A criterion asks that all members answer clearly and show they master the work, so a team where one person does the talking loses points; a student who contributed too little can also get a lower grade than the team.
